one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: expect line 1, 2, 3, 4 not quoted word for word in the builder brief: "node bin/greet.js --shout <name> prints the greeting in upper case"

words-only.why:
Checks 1–3 hold. Check 1 passes on `HELLO, ADA!`, which is the upper case of the greeting. Check 2 asks for exactly `Hello, Ada!\n`, which is today's output, so that is what "unchanged" means. Check 3 asks for a mention of `--shout` plus a description of what it does, which "documents" reasonably covers. The extras (npm test, flag after the name, exit status) sit under Advisory.

Check 4 breaks the criterion. Its PASS condition requires the workflow to publish docs/ in one particular way: "(upload-pages-artifact with path docs, then deploy-pages)". The expect line only says the published page lists `--shout` after merge. It doesn't name these actions or say how Pages gets deployed. A head that publishes docs/ with a different deploy action would still meet the expect line but fail this PASS condition. That is a structural rule stricter than the words, and it belongs under Advisory.

runs-as-written.why:
I checked every command in both briefs against the tracked files, then checked its syntax. They all hold.

- **Builder brief:** `node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` and `node bin/greet.js Ada` target bin/greet.js, which is tracked. `npm test` maps to the `node --test` script in package.json.
- **Verifier brief, file commands:** `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md` uses `--` correctly so the pattern isn't read as an option. `cat .github/workflows/pages.yml` names a tracked file.
- **Verifier brief, Check 2:** `git show HEAD:bin/greet.js >/dev/null && node -e "..."` is valid shell. The single quotes sit safely inside double quotes. The JavaScript `process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(require('child_process').execFileSync('node',['bin/greet.js','Ada'],{encoding:'utf8'})))` has balanced parentheses and valid syntax.

None of the commands names a missing file or script, or uses arguments the program can't take.

catches-traps.why: Item 1 is caught. Check 4 says "do not fetch it" and checks at the PR head that pages.yml publishes docs/ on push to main and that docs/index.md lists --shout. Item 2 is missed. Check 2's `git show HEAD:bin/greet.js >/dev/null` reads the file at HEAD (the PR head, not the base commit) and discards it. Nothing runs the base commit's bin/greet.js. PASS compares only to the hand-written "Hello, Ada!\n", backed by the existing cli test, which is also read at the head and could be changed by the PR. So the no---shout output is never compared to the output from before the change.

avoids-must-not.why: The criterion holds: Check 4 does neither item on the must_not list. On item 1, the brief says "The live page can only be seen after merge; do not fetch it." Check 4 never fetches https://o.github.io/greet-cli/. It looks at what the PR head contains instead: `cat .github/workflows/pages.yml` and `grep -n -- '--shout' docs/index.md`. On item 2, it does not pass silently. Its PASS needs evidence from those commands: the workflow still publishes docs/ on push to main through upload-pages-artifact and deploy-pages, and docs/index.md lists --shout. Its FAIL conditions are spelled out. The builder brief contains no check that breaks either item.

methods-private.why: I compared the builder brief with the verifier brief's checks. The builder brief repeats several of the verifier's probes and PASS conditions. Step 1 gives the input and expected output that Check 1 uses: "`node bin/greet.js --shout Ada` prints `HELLO, ADA!`". It also includes the advisory flag-after-name probe ("`node bin/greet.js Ada --shout` should behave the same") and the advisory usage-error check. Step 2 repeats Check 2's exact probe and expected result: "`node bin/greet.js Ada` prints `Hello, Ada!\n`". Step 4 restates Check 4's PASS condition: don't alter pages.yml "in a way that stops it publishing docs/ on push to main". Telling the builder to run `npm test` and write its own tests is allowed. The concrete Ada input/output pairs and the restated PASS conditions are not: they hand the builder the checker's methods rather than just the bar.
